answer: FINAL HYPOTHESIS (natural language, data-grounded): Among individuals who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed = 1, based on incarceration during 1985–1994) in this NLSY79-processed sample, median 1985 wealth (composite_wealth_1985) shows a clear racial disparity: White ever-incarcerated respondents held a median of $2,200, roughly 3–7 times the median of Black ($320, n=159) and Hispanic ($0, n=61) ever-incarcerated respondents. It also shows a sex disparity: female ever-incarcerated respondents had a $0 median (n=37) versus $1,000 for males (n=252), reflecting that 64.9% of ever-incarcerated females had zero wealth versus 35.7% of males. The race×sex cross runs from $0 (Black females, Hispanic females, Hispanic males) up to $2,000–$4,100 (White males and females). As supporting context, ever-incarcerated respondents overall held $720 median 1985 wealth vs $3,600 for never-incarcerated respondents (about 80% lower), and their median dropped to $0 by 1990 and 1996 while never-incarcerated medians grew to roughly $10,500 and $8,500. Sensitivity analysis shows the racial gap is substantially driven by higher zero-wealth shares among ever-incarcerated Black (43%) and Hispanic (48%) respondents versus White (23%): restricting to positive-wealth holders, medians become $4,400 (Black), $6,000 (Hispanic) and $6,000 (White); by sex, positive-wealth females ($7,000, n=11) exceed males ($5,475, n=148), reversing the headline sex gap, so the female $0 median is entirely a zero-wealth-share artifact. Because wealth is measured in 1985 while ever_jailed spans 1985–1994, these are associations/descriptive disparities among people later incarcerated — not evidence that incarceration caused the lower wealth — and the Hispanic (n≈61) and female (n≈37) subgroup findings are fragile given their small counts.

payload.hypothesis: Among individuals who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed = 1, 1985–1994), median 1985 wealth (composite_wealth_1985) shows a racial disparity — White ever-incarcerated respondents $2,200 vs Black $320 and Hispanic $0 (about 3–7x higher) — and a sex disparity (females $0 vs males $1,000), with race×sex medians from $0 (Black/Hispanic females) to $2,000–$4,100 (White respondents); the racial gap is largely driven by higher zero-wealth shares among Black (43%) and Hispanic (48%) vs White (23%) ever-incarcerated respondents, and ever-incarcerated respondents overall held $720 vs $3,600 for never-incarcerated.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013×6, no missing values). Main analysis: within ever_jailed==1 (n=289), median composite_wealth_1985 by race, by sex, and race×sex, with n, median, IQR, mean, zero/negative counts and bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, seeds). Context: ever-vs-never median diff with bootstrap CI, never-jailed splits, and temporal medians across 1985/1990/1996. Sensitivity: positive-wealth-only medians within ever-jailed to isolate zero-wealth share effects. All outputs saved to analysis/results/report.json; script: analysis/analysis_nls_incarceration.py.
